subject.title: Feature: fallbackChannel for hook mappings when primary delivery fails

question: Should hook mappings gain an explicit cross-channel fallback chain, and if so what privacy, retry-finality, account-selection, and duplicate-delivery rules must govern it?
rationale: The requested behavior introduces a new persisted configuration and delivery policy; source and documentation show that existing `channel: "last"` and failure destinations solve different problems.

options.title: Design a constrained fallback chain
options.body: Adopt ordered explicit destinations only after specifying opt-in routing, account ownership, retryable failure classes, and all-targets-failed reporting.

options.title: Keep one-target hook delivery
options.body: Retain the current single-destination contract and document failure notifications or operator recovery as the supported behavior.

options.title: Expose a plugin seam first
options.body: Add a generic post-send failure hook only if maintainers prefer extension-owned routing policy over a core hook-mapping option.

recommendation.title: Design a constrained fallback chain
recommendation.body: Adopt ordered explicit destinations only after specifying opt-in routing, account ownership, retryable failure classes, and all-targets-failed reporting.

likelyOwner.reason: He supplied the most recent substantive review of this exact hook and cron delivery boundary and has adjacent configuration-history evidence.
